units: millions of EUR (per-share values in EUR per ordinary share)
listing_note: Euronext Amsterdam ordinary listing; model built per ORDINARY SHARE in EUR (31.567m shares, 30-Jun-2026). The US OTC ADR (ADYEY) is 1 ADR = 1/100 ordinary: IV_per_ADR_USD = IV_per_ordinary_EUR x EURUSD / 100. Live cross-check 28-Aug-2026: EUR1079.6 x 1.1656 / 100 = $12.58 vs ADYEY traded $12.59 -- ratio confirmed.

inputs.share_count_basis: 31.567m ordinary shares at 30-Jun-2026 (H1-2026 letter). Held FLAT across the forecast: SBC is already fully expensed inside reported IFRS EBITDA, so compounding the share count as well would charge grant dilution twice. Observed historical drift is only ~0.647%/yr (30.5m FY2020 -> 31.567m Jun-2026) despite zero buybacks, so the flat-count convention is close to the realised outcome rather than a heroic assumption.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30-Jun-2026 = FY2025 43.457 + H1-2026 29.108 + H1-2026 cash-settled 0.316 - H1-2025 equity-settled 18.664 - ... ; headline TTM SBC 72.6m computed as FY2025 43.457 + (H1-2026 29.108 - H1-2025 18.664) x continuation. Filing sources: H1-2026 letter cash flow 'Equity-settled share-based compensation' 29,596k and 'Cash-settled share-based payment plan' 316k (EUR thousands); FY2025 annual report SBC EUR43.457m. Adyen discloses no separate equity-award withholding-tax line, so sbc_incl_equity_taxes equals the expense.
inputs.buyback_note: Adyen conducts ZERO buybacks and pays ZERO dividends -- 100% earnings retention. The flat share count is therefore a modelling convention the company has not funded with cash, not a repurchase-supported outcome. Mitigant: SBC is genuinely small (1.85% of net revenue vs 10-15% for US tech comparables) and realised dilution has run ~0.65%/yr.
inputs.notes:
MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, scenario-weighted -- routed via dcf-methods/SKILL.md as an operating company (payments platform / fintech infrastructure). A 10-year horizon is required because the year-5 owner-FCF margin (37.9% base) is still climbing toward its mature ~38.5% level; a 5-year build would capitalize an immature margin. This is the same horizon as the model of record (ADYEN_DCF_v1_preH1FY26.xlsx) and CORRECTS the 9-Aug-2026 published DCF, which used a 5-year horizon and consequently produced a weighted IV (EUR769.52) far below the model of record (EUR1,118.31) on nearly identical drivers.

MARGIN BASIS -- read before editing: assumptions.ebitda_margin_path is the REPORTED (post-SBC) EBITDA margin, because Adyen's IFRS operating expenses ALREADY contain share-based compensation. EBIT = EBITDA - D&A, and SBC is NOT deducted again. The sbc_pct_path rows are carried as an explicit, visible memo line (house rule that SBC is always its own line) and are used only for the street-basis add-back. This differs structurally from the model of record, whose row 7 is a PRE-SBC margin with SBC deducted separately -- both are internally consistent, but they are NOT interchangeable: pasting a pre-SBC margin path into this engine would understate the SBC charge by ~1.85% of revenue every year, and pasting this post-SBC path into the MOR engine would double-charge it.

NET CASH: headline balance-sheet cash of EUR12,392.8m at 30-Jun-2026 is overwhelmingly MERCHANT SETTLEMENT FLOAT and is NOT available to equity holders. Own cash = 12,392.8 - payables to merchants 8,097.4 + receivables from merchants/FI 602.8 = EUR4,898.2m, which ties to the H1-2026 letter's own statement of 'our cash stood at EUR4.9 billion' (line 524). The letter further states that net of the Talon.One and Orb acquisitions the balance would be 'approximately EUR4.6 billion'; since both closed 1-Jul-2026 and the EUR655.2m 'prepaid acquisition consideration' was already paid at the balance-sheet date, EUR4,600m is the correct forward own-cash figure. Net cash = 4,600 - 409.4 lease liabilities = EUR4,190m. Using the raw EUR12.4bn would overstate IV by roughly EUR260/share of merchants' money.

LEASES: treatment (A) -- lease liabilities (EUR409.4m: 338.3 non-current + 71.1 current) are deducted ONCE in the net-debt bridge, and lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows. TotalDebt is IFRS-16 leases only; Adyen carries no financial debt.

TWO INTEREST LINES -- do not conflate. (1) 'Net interest income' (H1-2026 EUR8.618m) is earned on embedded-finance products (Accounts, Capital) and is presented INSIDE net revenue: it is operating, recurs with volume, and is KEPT. (2) 'Finance income' (H1-2026 EUR143.229m; FY2025 EUR267.550m; TTM EUR272.1m) is interest on Adyen's OWN cash and sits below 'Income before net finance income'. It is STRIPPED from owner FCF, because the cash pile that generates it is separately added to the bridge as net cash -- leaving both in counts the cash twice.

MERCHANT FLOAT: valued SEPARATELY as a per-scenario addition (bear 988.0 / base 1,910.5 / bull 2,761.3), inherited unchanged from the model of record. This is the capitalized value of the spread Adyen earns on merchant balances it holds in transit. It is added to operating EV alongside net cash. Note this is NOT double-counting with the stripped Finance income: the stripped line is interest on Adyen's OWN EUR4.6bn, whereas the float stream is the economics of the merchants' EUR8.1bn, which never appears as own cash in the bridge.

WORKING CAPITAL is a net USE of cash and is SUBTRACTED. On a net-of-float basis, receivables from merchants/FI grow faster than trade payables as revenue compounds (H1-2026: receivables from merchants -40.1, trade and other receivables -28.6, trade and other payables -20.6, against inventories +27.3). A '+ working_capital' sign error inflated IV by ~EUR42-45m/yr before being caught on 9-Aug-2026; the sign here is negative and was re-verified against the H1-2026 cash flow statement.

RISK IS CHARGED ONCE, in the flows. All three scenarios use the SAME 10.5% WACC. Governance (CFO departure 31-Aug-2026, interim Hwa Tsao, Co-CEO health step-back), competition and integration risk are expressed through the bear case's driver paths and its 15% weight, NOT through a discount-rate premium. Stacking a WACC premium on probability-weighted scenarios would charge the same risk twice, and varying WACC by scenario would charge it a third time. This deliberately DIFFERS from the 9-Aug-2026 DCF, which used 9.0/10.0/11.5% by scenario.

historical_growth.revenue_basis: NetRevenue (Adyen reports net revenue as its top line; the CSV Revenue column is intentionally blank)
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (net revenue), used as the historical anchor; year-1 base growth is set at 20% reported, just below the 21-23% CC FY2026 guide, for FX drag
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' equity CAGR (29.9% 3yr / 34.1% 5yr) materially exceeds net revenue CAGR (21.1% / 28.1%). This is an artifact of 100% earnings retention -- zero dividends and zero buybacks mechanically compound book value faster than revenue -- and NOT evidence of superior returns on incremental capital. Equity CAGR is therefore explicitly REJECTED as the growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR (10.7% 3yr / 18.5% 5yr) sits far BELOW reported-FCF CAGR (21.2% / 25.6%). The gap is driven overwhelmingly by the Finance-income strip, not by SBC: interest on own cash rose from EUR29.3m in FY2022 to EUR246-350m in FY2023-25 as policy rates rose. That is a rate-cycle windfall on the cash pile, not operating performance, and it is precisely what must be removed to avoid double-counting the cash that is added back in the bridge. SBC is genuinely small (1.85% of net revenue). Owner FCF fell from EUR567.3m (FY2022) to EUR354.9m (FY2023) on the margin reset before recovering to EUR770.3m (FY2025) and EUR888.1m TTM.

scenario_narratives.base: Take-rate decline at 16.2bps is treated as MOSTLY benign volume tiering: net revenue keeps compounding with volume at a lower unit price, and unit economics hold, but a modest permanent drag is carried by letting growth decelerate slightly faster than volume through the decade. FY2026 growth of 20% reported sits just below the 21-23% CC guide (FX drag; the guide includes ~1pp of acquisition contribution). Margin follows management's own shape: ~1pp below FY2025 in 2026 on acquisition dilution and transaction costs, crossing the >55% 2028 target in year 3, then maturing near 57%. CapEx is 7% in year 1 exactly as guided, reverting to the historical 5% thereafter. Platforms (+37%) and Unified Commerce (+25%) keep mixing up against a slower Digital pillar.
scenario_narratives.bull: Digital's H1 improvement (+13%/+15% CC off a record-low Q1 +9%) proves to be a genuine structural reacceleration rather than a bounce; Platforms and Unified Commerce continue compounding in the 25-40% range and lift group growth toward the ~20% medium-term ambition for longer. Take-rate stabilizes at/above 16bps, confirming volume tiering over competitive discounting. The Talon.One/Orb pivot cross-sells successfully into Unified Commerce and Platforms, widening wallet share (disclosed <20% in years 3-7 rising to >40% after year 12), and further disciplined capital deployment extends the roadmap. Margin pulls the 55%+ target forward and matures near 59.6% on operating leverage over a fixed single-platform stack.
scenario_narratives.bear: 'Expected volume tiering' turns out to be competitive repricing: the June-2026 large-merchant pricing revision is the first of several, take rate keeps sliding below 16bps, and net revenue growth decouples downward from volume growth. Digital -- still ~55% of revenue -- stalls again after one good half against Stripe and Braintree's enterprise in-store push. The 7% CapEx step-up proves permanent rather than a one-year pull-forward, because AI-era infrastructure competition genuinely raised capital intensity; CapEx stays 5.5-6%. Margin expansion stalls far short of the 55% 2028 target. First-ever M&A integration risk crystallizes at exactly the moment the CFO departs and a Co-CEO has only recently returned to a visible operating role.

entry_price.method: Entry price = ( PV@15% of the 10 interim owner-FCFs + PV@15% of the terminal value + merchant float value + net cash ) / shares. The terminal value is computed at WACC (10.5%) because it is the fair price a buyer pays at exit; only the discounting back to today uses the 15% hurdle.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bull.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bear.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

entry_price.interpretation: The probability-weighted 15%-hurdle entry price of EUR888 is 17.7% below the current EUR1,079.60. A 15% IRR is therefore NOT available at today's price on these drivers; the base case clears roughly a 10.6% return. The bear-case entry price of EUR550 shows how far the hurdle falls short if the take-rate-compression path is the true one.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

sensitivity.note: Base-case value per share. Rows are WACC (8.5-12.5%), columns terminal growth (2.0-4.0%). House pair is WACC 10.5% / g 3.0% = EUR1,084.81 (centre cell). The two top-right cells are capped by the 20x terminal multiple, which is the cap doing its job -- Gordon would otherwise grant an exit multiple no buyer has to pay. Reverse read: the current EUR1,079.60 corresponds to a base-case WACC of almost exactly 10.5%, or equivalently to a ~1pp permanent haircut to the whole decade growth path.

growth_shift_sensitivity.note: Permanent parallel shift applied to EVERY year of the growth path, in all three scenarios; probability-weighted IV.
growth_shift_sensitivity.interpretation: Value is far more sensitive to a PERMANENT growth shift than to a one-year miss. A -1pp permanent shift lands at EUR1,086.77, essentially the current price -- so the market is pricing approximately a 1pp permanent haircut to Adyen's decade growth path. Break-even against EUR1,079.60 sits just past -1pp; a -3pp shift implies -10.3% downside.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35, restored deliberately from the 25/50/25 used on 9-Aug-2026 and matching the model of record. The 9-Aug run raised bear weight to 25% ahead of an uncertain H1 print; that print (13-Aug) landed clearly ahead -- 21% CC net revenue growth, 24% volume growth, guidance RAISED to 21-23% CC, Digital reaccelerating from its record-low Q1 -- which resolved the specific uncertainty the extra bear weight was insuring against. Bear stays at 15% and not lower because the take-rate question is genuinely unresolved (management's 'volume tiering' framing cannot yet be independently verified against competitive discounting) and because the balance sheet carries no solvency or refinancing risk at all -- the bear case is margin and growth compression, never distress. Bull at 35% because the bull path needs only the already-observed Platforms/Unified Commerce trajectory to persist, not several independent things to go right.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: Set to null deliberately. The house/street band is EUR1,152.69-EUR1,188.04, a spread of only 3.1%, because Adyen's SBC is 1.85% of net revenue rather than the 10-15% typical of US tech. The current price of EUR1,079.60 sits BELOW both bounds, so a band position would compute to roughly -207% -- a degenerate figure that says nothing useful. The finding is the narrowness itself: for Adyen the SBC accounting regime is almost irrelevant to the valuation, unlike a heavy issuer where it is most of the market cap.

wacc_rationale: 10.5% for ALL THREE scenarios, in the flows' own currency (EUR). Built from a ~2.6% 10-year Bund/EUR risk-free rate plus an equity risk premium of ~5.5% on a beta modestly above 1.0 for a high-multiple, long-duration growth asset, with a small increment for single-country listing and payments-competition dynamics. This matches the model of record's 10.5% exactly and is denominated consistently with Adyen's EUR reporting and EUR quote -- no USD-derived rate is used anywhere. Adyen carries no financial debt (only IFRS-16 leases), so WACC is effectively cost of equity. Crucially, the SAME rate is applied to bear, base and bull: risk is charged ONCE, in the probability-weighted flows. The 9-Aug-2026 DCF used 9.0/10.0/11.5% by scenario, which charged competition and governance risk twice (once in the bear driver paths, again in a higher bear discount rate) and materially widened the scenario spread for no economic reason. Governance risk (CFO departure, Co-CEO step-back) is expressed in the bear case's execution assumptions, NOT as a WACC premium.

valuation_philosophy.headline: Owner-FCF DCF on a 10-year explicit horizon, three scenarios probability-weighted at 15/50/35, all discounted at a single 10.5% EUR WACC.
valuation_philosophy.summary: Adyen is valued as what it is: a single-platform payments processor whose value is a long stream of free cash flow, not a bank and not a balance-sheet compounder. The engine projects net revenue, applies a reported (post-SBC) EBITDA margin path anchored to management's own guidance, subtracts D&A, taxes at a ramping cash rate, adds D&A back, subtracts capex and the working-capital use, and discounts the result. Three things about Adyen demand special handling and each is documented in inputs.notes: the cash on the balance sheet is mostly merchants' money and only EUR4.6bn is Adyen's; the income statement carries two different interest lines of which only one is operating; and the merchant float is a real economic asset valued separately from both.
principles: Owner FCF, not reported FCF: strip Finance income (interest on Adyen's own cash) because that cash is separately added to the bridge -- leaving both counts the pile twice.

Charge every cost exactly once. SBC is already inside IFRS EBITDA, so it is not deducted again and the share count is held flat. Lease liabilities are deducted once in the bridge, never also from the flows.
Charge risk exactly once, in the flows. One WACC across all three scenarios; governance and competition risk live in the bear case's drivers and its weight.
Only merchants' money that is actually Adyen's counts as net cash: EUR4.6bn own cash, not the EUR12.4bn headline.
Anchor year-1 to management's stated guidance, then let the drivers decay toward maturity over ten years -- long enough for the owner-FCF margin to actually mature before it is capitalized.
The terminal value is capped at 20x terminal FCF, so a small change in terminal growth cannot run the valuation away.
what_would_change_our_mind: Take rate stabilizing at or above 16bps for two consecutive halves would validate 'volume tiering' and shift weight toward the bull path; a slide below 15.5bps would do the reverse and is the single most important variable to watch.
CapEx failing to revert toward 5% in 2027 would confirm the bear case's reading that AI-era infrastructure raised capital intensity permanently.
Digital pillar growth stalling again after its H1-2026 improvement would undermine the base case, since Digital is still ~55% of revenue.
A permanent CFO appointment and evidence of clean Talon.One/Orb integration would remove the execution overhang currently expressed in the bear weight.

sanity_check.test_direction_note: ONE-DIRECTIONAL BY DESIGN. Adyen has de-rated monotonically since its 2018 IPO across every multiple. The historical averages below are hypergrowth-era artifacts and are explicitly NOT re-rating targets. This check can legitimately FAIL a model whose implied multiples sit ABOVE what the market has historically paid; it must NOT be read in the other direction -- the fact that today's multiples sit below every historical year is NOT by itself an argument that the stock is cheap, and no part of this valuation rests on such an argument. The DCF above stands on projected cash flows alone.

implied_multiples_base_case.note: Base-case implied equity value EUR34,258m against TTM net income 1,125.6, FY2025 equity 5,285.4, TTM net revenue 2,573.6 and TTM EBITDA 1,343.5. These are close to today's market multiples because the base case sits within 1% of the current price.

sanity_check.diagnosis: PASSED on the over-valuation test. Every base-case implied multiple sits BELOW even the cheapest year in Adyen's listed history (FY2025: P/E 40.8x, P/B 8.19x, EV/EBITDA 31.4x, P/S 18.3x): the model implies P/E 30.4x, P/B 6.48x, EV/EBITDA 20.9x and P/S 13.3x, and a terminal exit multiple of 13.7x EV/owner-FCF against a current market EV/owner-FCF of 31.5x. The model therefore assumes CONTINUED DE-RATING toward mature payments-platform multiples, not multiple expansion, and cannot be accused of importing a re-rating it has not earned. Per the one-directional rule, no inference is drawn in the opposite direction: the stock now trading at its cheapest multiples since listing is recorded as context, not as evidence of value.

model_of_record.note: Stephen's hand-checked framework; 10-year horizon, 10.5% WACC, 15/50/35 weights, float valued separately.

bridge.item: Horizon 5yr -> 10yr: the year-5 owner-FCF margin was still climbing, so the prior model capitalized an immature margin in perpetuity. This is the single largest correction and reconciles the prior DCF to the model of record.
bridge.note: Largest single term; absorbs the residual of the simultaneous re-solve.

Base revenue rolled forward FY2025 (2,364.2) -> TTM to 30-Jun-2026 (2,573.6)

reconciliation.bridge_note: Bridge items are APPROXIMATE attributions of a simultaneous re-solve, not a strictly sequential decomposition; they sum to the new weighted IV by construction. The dominant term by far is the horizon fix. The prior 9-Aug DCF was not merely stale -- at a 5-year horizon it disagreed with the model of record by EUR349/share on nearly identical drivers, and that gap was a methodology error rather than a difference of judgment.

judgement_calls.take_rate: RESOLVED AS MOSTLY BENIGN, WITH A DELIBERATE HAIRCUT. The base case treats the 16.8 -> 16.2bps decline primarily as volume tiering: net revenue compounds with volume at a lower unit price while unit economics hold. The supporting evidence is that H1 volume grew 24% while net revenue grew 21% CC -- a genuine competitive repricing would have opened a far wider gap -- and that customer concentration is IMPROVING (top 300 customers now ~60% of growth, down from >70% three years ago), which is inconsistent with discounting to retain large accounts. But management's framing cannot yet be independently verified, so the base case does not treat it as fully benign: base growth decelerates slightly faster than volume through the decade (20% -> 7.5%) rather than tracking it. The bear case takes the opposite view outright -- sustained take-rate compression decoupling revenue from volume, growth collapsing to 11% by year 2. This is the single most important unresolved variable in the valuation and is the first item in key_metrics_to_watch.
judgement_calls.capex: MODELLED AS GUIDED IN BASE AND BULL, PERMANENTLY HIGHER IN BEAR. Base and bull carry 7% in year 1 exactly as management frames it -- a pull-forward of 2027 datacenter spend to secure compute amid supply-chain constraints -- reverting to the historical 5% from year 2. The bear case deliberately does NOT accept that framing: it holds capex at 6.0% in year 2 and 5.5-5.8% thereafter, on the reading that AI-era infrastructure competition has genuinely stepped up capital intensity and the 'one-year pull-forward' is a characterization rather than a fact. H1-2026 capex was only 5% of net revenue, implying a very sharp H2 step-up to reach the full-year 7% -- worth verifying at the FY2026 print.
judgement_calls.ma_pivot: BULL CREDITS FURTHER DEPLOYMENT; BEAR CARRIES INTEGRATION RISK. The bull case gives credit for the Talon.One/Orb strategy widening wallet share (disclosed at <20% in years 3-7 rising to >40% after year 12) and for further disciplined capital deployment, expressed as a slower growth decay -- 10.5% still in year 10 versus 7.5% in the base. The bear case treats ~EUR1.05bn deployed for ~1pp of 2026 growth as a poor initial return and charges integration risk through stalled margin expansion (52.7% terminal, far short of the 55% 2028 target). Balance-sheet treatment is symmetric and is the important mechanical point: net cash is marked DOWN to the post-acquisition EUR4.6bn the company itself states, so the cash spent is removed from the bridge in every scenario while only bull and base credit the growth it buys.
judgement_calls.governance: NO WACC PREMIUM -- CHARGED IN THE FLOWS INSTEAD. The CFO departure (31-Aug-2026, interim Hwa Tsao, permanent search ongoing), the Co-CEO's health-related step-back, the new CPO and APAC succession together represent unusually concentrated turnover for a founder-culture company, and this is real risk. It is charged through the bear case's execution assumptions and its 15% weight, NOT through the discount rate. Adding a WACC premium on top of probability-weighted scenarios would charge the same risk twice, and using a higher WACC in the bear case than the bull would charge it a third time -- which is exactly what the 9-Aug-2026 DCF did with its 9.0/10.0/11.5% scenario spread. Mitigating evidence weighed: van der Does co-hosted the H1 call, his visible return to an investor-facing role, and the print itself was strong.
